title: Shankar Mahadevan's Malgudi Brings Its South Indian Resto-Café to Delhi
excerpt: The pure-vegetarian café co-founded by the Padma Shri singer-composer opens its first capital outlet in Rajouri Garden, with a filter kaapi bar, an open kitchen and a Mulbagal dosa made to a century-old recipe.
body:
• Malgudi, the South Indian resto-café co-founded by singer-composer Shankar Mahadevan and K. S. Ramakrishnan of Eatopia, has opened its first Delhi outlet in Rajouri Garden.
  • The pure-vegetarian format centres on a Filter Kaapi Barista Station and an open kitchen, with dishes built from family and regional recipes.
  • Signature items include the Mulbagal Legacy Dosa, Ven Pongal Arancini, Bisi Bele Bibimbap and Sri Lankan Tamil Curry with Idiyappam.
  • The brand already runs outlets in Mumbai and the UAE, with Gurugram due next — Delhi is its first step into the capital.

Delhi has a new address for filter kaapi and hundred-year-old dosa recipes. Malgudi, the South Indian resto-café co-founded by singer-composer Shankar Mahadevan and entrepreneur K. S. Ramakrishnan, has opened in Rajouri Garden — the brand's first outlet in the capital — as it expands beyond Mumbai and the UAE, according to Restaurant India. ThePrint first reported the opening.

"This brand is deeply personal to me because it celebrates the food and memories I grew up with."

— Shankar Mahadevan, Co-founder, Eatopia

What the Rajouri Garden Outlet Looks Like

The format is an all-day resto-café rather than a quick-service counter: an open kitchen, a dedicated Filter Kaapi Barista Station where the davara pour is part of the theatre, and a room dressed in terracotta hues, brass lighting, cane-backed chairs and teak tables, with hand-painted murals and Chettinad-style tilework, as Hotelier India describes the concept. The design deliberately leans warm and nostalgic — a traditional wooden swing, coastal and temple-town references — rather than the moody minimalism of most new Delhi openings. The outlet is at D-4, Ring Road, opposite Pillar No. 184 in Rajouri Garden.

Beyond Dosa and Idli

The menu's anchor is the Mulbagal Legacy Dosa, made to a century-old recipe — crisp at the edges, soft inside — alongside Ghee Podi Thatte Idli. The kitchen's signature move is reinterpretation: Ven Pongal Arancini takes a Tamil comfort dish into Italian form, and Bisi Bele Bibimbap recasts Karnataka's spiced rice in a Korean stone-pot format. Larger plates include Paneer Ghee Roast with Neer Dosa, a Sri Lankan Tamil Curry served with Idiyappam, and Sanchi's Vegetable Stew with Appam. Kaki's Sheera closes the meal. The restaurant is pure vegetarian, with vegan and gluten-free options across the menu.

Early visitor accounts single out the Mulbagal Dosa and the idiyappam curry, and Hindustan Times' visit found the food, drinks and nostalgic room impressive, according to a review summary of the Delhi opening.

The Brand Behind It

Malgudi runs under Eatopia, founded by Ramakrishnan, Mahadevan's longtime friend and business partner. The brand operates four outlets in Mumbai and two in the UAE, and a Gurugram outlet is due to open soon — which matters for the diaspora in both directions: UAE diners already know the name from Dubai, and Delhi is the test of whether a Mumbai-born, celebrity-fronted South Indian format can win in a city with deep loyalties to its own dosa institutions.

Ramakrishnan framed the launch as a community play: a space that feels welcoming while staying true to the diversity of South Indian cuisine. Mahadevan's pitch is simpler — the response at earlier outlets convinced the partners that South Indian food, served with its stories attached, travels well beyond the south.
